The 'Add Top Tier Candidates' candidate-selection option can NEVER be applied -- canopy and cascor disagree on the value vocabulary. canopy's cn-candidate-selection-radio declares {'label': 'Add Top Tier Candidates', 'value': 'top_tier'} at juniper-canopy/src/frontend/dashboard_manager.py:1471; cascor's API accepts only Literal['top','random','mixed'] at juniper-cascor/src/api/models/training.py:159 and :327. No translation exists on the canopy side -- _toggle_cn_selection_inputs_handler (dashboard_manager.py:6815-6821) consumes 'top_tier' purely for UI enable/disable gating and the raw value goes into the apply payload. LIVE INSTANCE: select 'Add Top Tier Candidates', set a consistent triple (S=5,T=5,R=0 -- clientside validator satisfied, feedback empty), click Apply -> 'Failed to apply (HTTP 502): Backend rejected parameters: [{type: literal_error, loc: [body, candidate_selection], msg: "Input should be top, random or mixed", input: top_tier}]'. CONTROL: the sibling arm 'random' matches cascor's literal exactly and applied cleanly in the same session ('Parameters applied'; backend candidate_selection=random, selected_candidates=5, top_candidates=0, random_candidates=5). So one of the two shipped options is permanently unusable. Also note cascor's third literal 'mixed' has no canopy UI option at all. Fix target: map top_tier->top at the payload boundary (or change the option value), and consider surfacing 'mixed'.

A SUCCESSFUL parameter apply is reported to the operator as a 502 failure whenever the sidebar's nn_max_total_epochs has gone stale against cascor's epochs_max. Two-part chain, both halves live-verified. (a) CASCOR SIDE: PATCH /v1/training/params silently ignores epochs_max -- 'curl -X PATCH ... -d {"epochs_max": 115000}' returns HTTP 200 status=success while the stored value stays 140795. Control: the same request shape with {"patience": 77} stored 77 correctly, so the silent-ignore is specific to epochs_max, which cascor owns/recomputes. (b) CANOPY SIDE: cascor_service_adapter._verify_apply_roundtrip (juniper-canopy/src/backend/cascor_service_adapter.py:~1316-1334) compares ALL mapped keys after the write and, on ANY divergence, returns {'ok': False, 'error': 'verification_failed'} for the WHOLE apply -- discarding the fact that every other key landed. LIVE INSTANCE: canopy logged 'apply_params verify mismatch: {epochs_max: {requested: 115000, applied: 140795}}' -> UI showed 'Failed to apply (HTTP 502) ... verification_failed', yet cascor really did take the user's edits (output_epochs=12345 and the S/T/R triple were all present afterwards and survived a page reload). The operator is told their change failed when it succeeded, and would reasonably retry. TRIGGER IS PRECISE: only when the sidebar's seeded nn_max_total_epochs differs from cascor's live epochs_max -- i.e. after cascor has moved it, which happens across a training run. A page reload re-seeds the sidebar (140795) and the next apply succeeds. WHY EARLIER SEGMENTS MISSED IT: W3-03 (run 20260811T010700Z) drove /api/set_params with a body seeded from live /api/state, so no key could diverge. Fix target: exclude cascor-owned keys from the round-trip verify, or degrade a single-key mismatch to the existing 'mismatches' partition instead of failing the whole apply.

The user cannot fix it in place from the shipped state because T and R both ship disabled=True behind cn-multi-candidate-checkbox; the recovery is to change S, or to enable multi-candidate and edit T/R. Related observation (not itself a defect, since the matrix documents the radio as shipping value=None): cascor's candidate_selection is never seeded into cn-candidate-selection-radio on page load, so with multi_candidate=True seeded from the backend the checkbox shows checked and the radio is ungated (opacity 1) yet neither option is selected and both count inputs stay disabled until the user picks one.

Could not settle the open question this segment, and the reason is itself the finding: the naive process count is CONTAMINATED on this shared box. 'pgrep -f JuniperCascor1.*forkserver' returned 18 at +43 s and +73 s after a clean stop (apparently reproducing the original observation), then 7, then 3, then ROSE BACK to 11 -- a rise that is impossible for a draining pool and exposed the error. Attributing by parentage instead: my leg (pid 298210) held exactly 2 children -- 319149 (14 MB) and the 476 MB multiprocessing forkserver 319150 -- and NO candidate-pool grandchildren, i.e. my pool had fully drained. The 461 MB x7 cluster belonged to a DIFFERENT cascor (pid 348136, started 130 s earlier by a concurrent session). The forkserver process itself persisting is expected and is not pool residency. METHOD FOR THE NEXT ATTEMPT: record the leg pid at bring-up and count only its descendants (pgrep -P / ppid walk), never a box-wide pattern match. The original F-CASCOR-003b observation was taken with the box-wide method and should be re-taken before being treated as real.
